title: Receiver UID is still hash(name) in several places — marked TODO for future static-UID migration
answers: Where does the code still assume a receiver's UID equals a hash of its name?
What needs to change when receivers get independently-persisted UIDs instead of name-derived ones?
Which call sites break if receiver UID is no longer deterministic from name?
body: PostableApiReceiver/models.Receiver now carry a real persisted UID (via ResourceMetadata / legacy_storage.ReceiverToPostableApiReceiver), but several call sites still compute the UID as v1.ReceiverUID(name)/legacy_storage.NameToUid(name) and are marked with `// TODO: This won't work with static UIDs.` comments: pkg/services/ngalert/api/api_alertmanager.go:ReceiverStatus.GetUID, pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/alertmanager_config.go:cleanPermissions, pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/routes.go:ResetUserDefinedRoute, pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/receiver_svc.go:GetReceivers/CreateReceiver. When receivers move to independently-persisted (non-name-derived) UIDs, grep for these TODOs — they are the remaining surface that must change together.
applies: Future work that decouples receiver UID from its name (static/persisted UIDs).
says: Which code paths compute receiver ID by hashing the name?
Several locations still derive receiver ID from receiver name.
What code breaks when receiver IDs aren't name-derived anymore?
Receiver ID generation from name needs to change for persistence.
Where is receiver ID still being calculated from name?
